entry_state: Option premium, intrinsic gains and related protection cost are separate. Actual strike and designated risk determine different calculations; cumulative component reserves preserve mismatch reversals and hypothetical options create no cash or asset. The next subsection has introduced a zero-cost collar with purchased call and written put, whose gross premiums offset; its valuation continues next.
exit_state: The matched zero-cost collar retains signed interim reserves and gross cash movements. Forward components require an explicit election. Rebalancing retains each layer's original date and price, recognizes existing ineffectiveness first, and applies the lower-of rule cumulatively. The add-only worked method is bounded; removed volumes and changed instruments need their own rules.
findings: The collar's supplied marks have separate mathematical witnesses, explicitly not estimated probabilities or a transition model.
The collar equations retain positive asset/liability values and a negative written-put sign, producing the clipped terminal inventory cost.
Rebalancing examples show a balanced but wrong journal when cumulative measurements are restarted. Layer origins and previously recognized ineffectiveness survive additions.
No new confirmed local defect; the general signed-component and changed-instrument methods remain separate requirements.
